title: What If Every Nuclear Plant Shut Down Tomorrow?

scenes.text: What if every nuclear power plant shut down tomorrow? One country would lose two thirds of its electricity.
There are about 443 reactors running worldwide. Together they make about nine percent of the world's electricity.
That's roughly 2,700 terawatt-hours a year. It went up again in 2025.
France would feel it most: about 68 percent of its electricity comes from nuclear. Slovakia, 64. Ukraine, 52. Hungary, 45.
Those grids would have to find that power fast, from imports, gas or coal, or go dark.
Nine percent doesn't sound like much. But no other source could cover it overnight.
